records.description: Brand, retailer, and commerce provider are three independent facts and must never collapse into one another: a Nike jacket sold by Farfetch, surfaced through provider-X, must report retailer = Farfetch, not Nike and not provider-X.
records.notes: Section 14 required example. SYNTHETIC: brand/retailer/provider co-occurring this cleanly wasn't observed in a single real record, but each field individually is a real, distinct field (RecommendedProduct.brand, .retailer alias-chain target, .source) per supabase/functions/scan-identify/shoppingProvider.ts:15-45.

records.description: When a provider names a merchant but no explicit retailer field, the merchant IS the seller — this is an audited semantic mapping (merchant == retailer-of-record), not a brand fallback.
records.notes: Section 14 required example. SYNTHETIC composition; 'merchant' as a real alias field is cited in the census (components/ProductShelf.tsx getRetailer candidate list, services/dressingRoomCommerce.ts normalizer). Doctrine: reading merchant as the seller is a deliberate, audited mapping — it is NOT the same operation as falling back to brand (Finding F1), because merchant genuinely denotes a seller-shaped field, whereas brand denotes the manufacturer.

records.description: A record with a known brand but no retailer, merchant, store, or source field at all must report the seller as UNKNOWN — never substitute the brand.
records.notes: Section 14 required example (doctrine target, not current behavior). See Finding F1 in docs/commerce-corpus/01-commerce-shape-census.md: 2 of 4 real call sites (components/ProductShelf.tsx:167 getRetailer; services/dressingRoomCommerce.ts persisted normalizer) currently fall back to brand and WOULD violate this expected outcome; see ri-fallback-divergence-finding below for the reproduction of that exact behavior.

records.description: A record with a known commerce provider/source but no retailer, brand, merchant, or store field must never silently display the provider name as if it were the retailer.
records.notes: Section 14 required example (doctrine target). Real source explicitly documents 'source' as a provider identity that must never be a ranking input (supabase/functions/scan-identify/canonicalCommerce.ts:20-21 comment on CanonicalOffer.source) — this fixture extends that same neutrality principle to display: a provider name is not a retailer name. Note: this is the doctrine target; per Finding F1, real fallback chains DO read 'source' as a last-resort retailer candidate, which is a softer, more defensible fallback than the brand-substitution case (a provider string is at least sometimes literally the retailer's own name, e.g. 'poshmark'), but is still not a verified retailer identity and should be flagged distinctly from a truly resolved retailer.

records.description: Reproduces Finding F1: the exact same raw commerce record, run through the three real retailer-resolution call sites that exist in source today, produces THREE DIFFERENT results for 'who is the retailer'. This scenario documents current (non-doctrine-compliant) behavior for regression-tracking, not the desired outcome.

callSites.name: normalizePurchaseOptions (persisted)
callSites.violation: substitutes brand for retailer, and does so before checking source

callSites.name: mapRawProductToPurchaseOption
callSites.violation: substitutes provider name for retailer (softer than brand-substitution, still not a verified retailer)

callSites.name: mapLegacyToV2 similarFinds mapping
callSites.violation: same as above; still not the one call site that leaves retailer genuinely unknown in this particular input (that path only leaves it unknown when source is ALSO absent)
